messages.author: 50b36e864fb52ac0
messages.subject: Comparison in phylogenetic signal
parts:
Hello all! I am trying to figure out which out of two landmarking hypothesis is more likely, and I believe (based on conversation with people I've had in this googlegroup) that the strength of phylogenetic signal is a good way to study this.
As I understand it, comparing the results of the phy.signal function between the two landmarking hypothesis is not a good way to go about this. So a different method must be used.
Dr. Michael Collyer pointed out to me that this has been done before (not comparing different landmarking hypothesis, but comparing different traits), quite recently in fact, in a work published by him (Collyer, Baken and Adams, 2021).
I have been trying to understand how to use this method, but it is currently beyond my understanding, both in statistics and programming knowledge.
What I understand is, that a non-parametric permutation test for the log-likelihood of an evolutionary model is performed, which delivers a standardized statistic termed Z, which is useful for comparing phylogenetic signals. What I gather is that this test relies on the generation of a null-hypothesis based on random residuals generated in a permutation procedure (using the RRPP package) based on the data. This null hypothesis represents a scenario in which there is no phylogenetic signal, as I understand it.
An additional layer of complexity for me, is that in the manuscript, data consisting of a single measurement was used (surface area to volume ratio, and relative body width), and I am trying to find a way to use this method for morphometric data. I am sure it is not quite as complicated as it seems to me, but nonetheless, the solution still eludes me.

I also wonder if it is possible to use a similar method to compare between other things besides phylogenetic signals, such as procrustes distances or evolutionary rates.

I have been trying to understand the code used in the manuscript (which can be found in Supporting Information), but I am having trouble with it. I will continue to read and educate myself on these topics, but any help or advice in this matter that would point me in the right direction would be truly appreciated.

messages.author: 4d71c6e24fb21497
messages.subject: RE: [geomorph-r-package] Comparison in phylogenetic signal
parts:
Vicente,

 

I think the logic breaks down at the first step: using phylogenetic signal to determine which landmarking hypothesis is more likely. This does not make sense. Phylogenetic signal is the degree to which variation across taxa associate with their phylogenetic relationships. Having one landmarking scheme ‘fitting’ the phylogeny cannot be taken as evidence that it is a better landmarking approach as far as I can see. There are many reasons why some data may or may not fit a phylogeny, and they have very little to do with the way the landmarks are taken.

 

In other words, there are a great deal of assumptions in the claim that a better fit of the data to the phylogeny is a better landmarking scheme.

 

I would suggest a conceptual rethink of what you are trying to do, and why.

 

Dean
